standard.name: attained pseudo-true projection in misspecified conditional moments
Hölder source condition with Tikhonov qualification two

assumptions.condition: \(\forall k\in\mathcal K:\ \mathcal H_k\subset L_X\text{ is closed}\).
\(|Y|\vee\sup_{k\in\mathcal K}\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_k}|h(X)|\vee\sup_{k\in\mathcal K}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_k}|f(Z)|\le B\quad P\text{-a.s.}\).

novel.justification: This holds for candidate critics contained in the closure of the conditional-expectation range, since the least-squares pseudo-true residual is orthogonal to that range. Sieve critics made from conditional expectations of target-basis functions give a concrete implementation.

assumptions.condition: \(\forall k\in\mathcal K:\ (h_{k,\ell})_{\ell\ge1}\subset\mathcal H_k\text{ is fixed and dense in }\mathcal H_k\text{ under }\|\cdot\|_{L_2(P_X)}\).

novel.justification: Fixed countable neural-network or sieve dictionaries with rational coefficients are dense in their separable closures. Fixing the enumeration before observing the sample makes an implementable deterministic tie-break possible.

assumptions.condition: \(\forall(k,\lambda,\ell)\in\mathcal K\times\Lambda_n\times\mathbb N:\ A_{k,\lambda,\ell}\text{ is Borel measurable}\).

\(\forall(k,\lambda)\in\mathcal K\times\Lambda_n:\ h\mapsto\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_k}\{2P_{\mathrm{tr}}[(Y-h(X))f(Z)]-P_{\mathrm{tr}}f(Z)^2\}+\lambda P_{\mathrm{tr}}h(X)^2\text{ is lower semicontinuous on }\mathcal H_k\).

novel.justification: Finite sieves and rationally parameterized continuous neural classes with compact parameter closure have lower-semicontinuous empirical objectives. This primitive regularity lets a fixed dense dictionary approximate the empirical infimum without selecting a nonmeasurable optimizer.

It is satisfied when the empirical criterion is lower semicontinuous along the fixed dense dictionary and the dictionary is chosen to be criterion-dense, as for finite sieves and rationally parameterized continuous neural classes with compact parameter closure. It rules out a nonconstructive optimizer without assuming a statistical rate.

This proposal-specific truncation condition only requires the displayed finite grid to reach the continuous oracle scale. With \(J_n=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\), it follows elementarily if \(s_{k,n}\ge2^{-(1+\bar\beta)}n^{-(1+\bar\beta)}\) for every candidate, which is directly checkable from the declared scale.
The explicit Assouad handle needs a nonempty high-frequency block. Its displayed dimension formula satisfies this eventually for fixed positive \(R\) and sufficiently small \(c_0\).

definitions.name: Target approximation and witness deficiency
definitions.construction: \(h_{\mathcal H,k}^\dagger=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{h\in\mathcal H_k}\|h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}\), \(\varepsilon_{H,k}=\|h_{\mathcal H,k}^\dagger-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}\), \(D_{\mathcal F_k}(q)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_k}\{2E_P[q(Z)f(Z)]-E_P[f(Z)^2]\}\), and \(\varepsilon_{F,k}^2=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_k}\{\|q_h-q_{h^\dagger}\|_{L_2(P_Z)}^2-D_{\mathcal F_k}(q_h-q_{h^\dagger})\}_+\).

definitions.name: Explicit measurable training TRAE path
definitions.construction: For \(k\in\mathcal K,\lambda\in\Lambda_n,\ell\ge1\), set \(A_{k,\lambda,\ell}=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_k}\{2P_{\mathrm{tr}}[(Y-h_{k,\ell}(X))f(Z)]-P_{\mathrm{tr}}[f(Z)^2]\}+\lambda P_{\mathrm{tr}}[h_{k,\ell}(X)^2]\) and \(a_{k,\lambda}=\inf_{\ell\ge1}A_{k,\lambda,\ell}\). On \(\{\exists\ell:A_{k,\lambda,\ell}\le a_{k,\lambda}+n^{-1}\}\), let \(\widehat\ell_{k,\lambda}=\min\{\ell\ge1:A_{k,\lambda,\ell}\le a_{k,\lambda}+n^{-1}\}\); on its complement set \(\widehat\ell_{k,\lambda}=1\). Define \(\widehat h_{k,\lambda}=h_{k,\widehat\ell_{k,\lambda}}\).

definitions.name: Observable split-sample validation selector
definitions.construction: \(\widehat V_{k,\lambda}=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_k}\{2P_{\mathrm{va}}[(Y-\widehat h_{k,\lambda}(X))f(Z)]-P_{\mathrm{va}}[f(Z)^2]\}+\lambda P_{\mathrm{va}}[\widehat h_{k,\lambda}(X)^2]\), \(\operatorname{pen}_{k,\lambda}=8B^2\sqrt{\log(4K|\Lambda_n|/\eta)/n_{\mathrm{va}}}\), and \((\widehat k,\widehat\lambda)\) is the lexicographically least minimizer of \(\widehat V_{k,\lambda}+\operatorname{pen}_{k,\lambda}\) on \(\mathcal K\times\Lambda_n\); set \(\widehat h=\widehat h_{\widehat k,\widehat\lambda}\).

definitions.name: Bounded two-coordinate domain-separation construction
definitions.construction: Let \(U,V,\xi\) be mutually independent Rademacher variables, set \(Z=X=(U,V)\) and \(Y=a_0U+b_0V+\xi\). Take \(\mathcal H^\circ=\{aU+bV:|a|\vee|b|\le1/4\}\), \(\mathcal F_1^\circ=\{sU+tV:|s|\vee|t|\le1\}\), and \(\mathcal F_2^\circ=\{sU:|s|\le1\}\).

definitions.name: Quantified diagonal Assouad handle
definitions.construction: Set \(m_n=\lfloor(R^2n/(16c_0^2))^{1/(2a+2s+1)}\rfloor\), \(\sigma_j=j^{-a}\), \(\gamma_n=c_0(m_n/2)^a/\sqrt n\), \(\Theta_{s,R,m_n}=\{u\in\mathbb R^{m_n}:\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}j^{2s}u_j^2\le R^2\}\), and \(B_n=\{\lceil m_n/2\rceil,\ldots,m_n\}\). For \(\omega\in\{-1,1\}^{|B_n|}\), set \(\theta_j^\omega=\gamma_n\omega_j\) on \(B_n\) and zero otherwise. In independent halves observe \(G_j^{\mathrm{tr}}=\sigma_j\theta_j+\sqrt{2/n}\zeta_j^{\mathrm{tr}}\) and \(G_j^{\mathrm{va}}=\sigma_j\theta_j+\sqrt{2/n}\zeta_j^{\mathrm{va}}\), with independent standard Gaussian noises. For \(k=0,\ldots,m_n\), let \(\mathcal H_{k,m_n}=\{u\in\Theta_{s,R,m_n}:u_j=0\text{ for }j>k\}\) and \(\mathcal F_{k,m_n}=\{f\in\mathbb R^{m_n}:f_j=0\text{ for }j\in B_n\}\). Thus \(\mathcal H_{m_n,m_n}=\Theta_{s,R,m_n}\) and every witness annihilates \(B_n\). Define \(\mathcal L^{\mathrm{tr}}_{k,\lambda}(u,f)=2\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}(G_j^{\mathrm{tr}}-\sigma_ju_j)f_j-\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}f_j^2+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}u_j^2\), with \(\mathcal L^{\mathrm{va}}_{k,\lambda}\) obtained by replacing \(G_j^{\mathrm{tr}}\) by \(G_j^{\mathrm{va}}\). Let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the Borel maps that choose a training minimizer for every finite \((k,\lambda)\) path and the lexicographically least validation-score minimizer. For \(\theta=\theta^\omega\), \(\varepsilon_{H,k}^2=\sum_{j>k}(\theta_j^\omega)^2\), \(\varepsilon_{H,m_n}=0\), and \(\varepsilon_{F,m_n}^2\ge\sum_{j\in B_n}\sigma_j^2(\theta_j^\omega)^2\ge|B_n|\sigma_{m_n}^2\gamma_n^2\). At \(\lambda=m_n^{-2a}\), \(\varepsilon_{F,m_n}^2/\lambda\ge|B_n|\gamma_n^2\). Neighboring Gaussian alternatives have Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(2c_0^2\). The Handle is Assouad comparison under \(\mathcal R_n(\widehat\theta,\theta)=E_\theta\|\widehat\theta-\theta\|_2^2\).

statements.statement: For the conditional-expectation operator \(T\), \(\|T(h-h')\|_{L_2(P_Z)}\le\|h-h'\|_{L_2(P_X)}\) for all \(h,h'\in L_X\).
statements.justification: Jensen contraction gives the needed continuity without a separate continuity assumption.
statements.gap: This is a derived property of conditional expectation rather than a restriction imposed by TRAE or RDIV.
statements.consumer: It supplies the continuity step for the pseudo-true and approximation geometry.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{ass:pseudotrue-attainment}\), \(\texttt{ass:target-closed}\), and \(\texttt{ass:target-convex}\), \(h^\dagger\) in \(\texttt{def:pseudotrue-target}\) and every \(h_{\mathcal H,k}^\dagger\) in \(\texttt{def:misspecification}\) are uniquely defined.
statements.justification: Both defect coordinates require unique reference points.
statements.gap: The argument uses Hilbert-space metric projections rather than an unspecified pseudo-true witness.
statements.consumer: It makes the candidate-specific approximation coordinates reproducible.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{ass:split}\), \(\texttt{ass:finite-candidates}\), \(\texttt{ass:target-origin}\), \(\texttt{ass:witness-nonempty}\), \(\texttt{ass:witness-star}\), \(\texttt{ass:bounded-envelope}\), \(\texttt{ass:dense-enumeration}\), \(\texttt{ass:training-evaluation-measurable}\), \(\texttt{ass:criterion-lsc}\), \(\texttt{ass:validation-score-measurable}\), and \(\texttt{ass:enumeration-infimum}\), the least-index map \(\widehat\ell_{k,\lambda}\) in \(\texttt{def:trae-path}\) is measurable and \(A_{k,\lambda,\widehat\ell_{k,\lambda}}\le a_{k,\lambda}+n^{-1}\) almost surely. Consequently every \(\widehat h_{k,\lambda}\) and holdout score is measurable, finite, and the lexicographic validation selector is a measurable finite argmin.
statements.justification: The selector is an explicit measurable algorithm, not an appeal to an unverified measurable-selection theorem.
statements.gap: Existing TRAE analyses may state an approximate optimizer abstractly; the countable least-index construction fixes an implementable version for validation.
statements.consumer: It makes the selected estimator a legitimate random element for high-probability oracle analysis.

statements.statement: Under the member conditions of \(\mathcal M_n\) and \(\texttt{ass:source}\), the measurable observable selector in \(\texttt{def:validation-selector}\) should satisfy, with probability at least \(1-\eta\), \[\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\le C\inf_{k\in\mathcal K,\lambda\in\Lambda_n}\left\{\lambda^{\bar\beta}+\frac{\delta_{k,n}^2+\varepsilon_{H,k}^2+\varepsilon_{F,k}^2+B^2\sqrt{\log(4K|\Lambda_n|/\eta)/n_{\mathrm{va}}}}{\lambda}\right\},\] and \[\|T(\widehat h-h^\dagger)\|_{L_2(P_Z)}^2\le C\inf_{k\in\mathcal K,\lambda\in\Lambda_n}\left\{\lambda^{\bar\beta}+\delta_{k,n}^2+\varepsilon_{H,k}^2+\varepsilon_{F,k}^2+B^2\sqrt{\log(4K|\Lambda_n|/\eta)/n_{\mathrm{va}}}\right\}.\] Here \(\delta_{k,n}\) uses candidate radii at allocation \(\eta/(2K|\Lambda_n|)\), so the training event is simultaneous over every \((k,\lambda)\). Under \(\texttt{ass:iv-validity}\) and \(\texttt{ass:completeness}\), \(h^\dagger=h_0\); absent that calibration, \(h^\dagger\) is only the stated pseudo-true sensitivity target.
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing proposed result: an observable model-pair and regularization selector with separate target and witness defects.
statements.gap: Tan and Syrgkanis (2026, Theorem 3.13 and Remark 3.8) use realizability and exact witness closeness. Li et al. (2024, Theorem 12 and Section 8) validate misspecified RDIV with an explicit learned operator, not an implicit adversarial critic that omits residual coordinates.
statements.consumer: If proved, it supplies computable joint class selection for NPIV and proximal bridge estimation with imperfect target and critic sieves.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{ass:iv-validity}\) and \(\texttt{ass:completeness}\), \(h^\dagger=h_0\) is defined without \(\texttt{ass:pseudotrue-attainment}\). If some \(k_0\in\mathcal K\) satisfies \(h_0\in\mathcal H_{k_0}\) and \(D_{\mathcal F_{k_0}}(q_h-q_{h_0})=\|q_h-q_{h_0}\|_{L_2(P_Z)}^2\) for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{k_0}\), then \(\varepsilon_{H,k_0}=\varepsilon_{F,k_0}=0\). If also \(\texttt{ass:grid-coverage}\) holds, the strong-error display proposed in \(\texttt{conj:validated-misspecified-trae}\) is bounded by \(C\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}\{\lambda^{\bar\beta}+s_{k_0,n}/\lambda\}\le C s_{k_0,n}^{\bar\beta/(1+\bar\beta)}\). When the holdout scale is no larger than \(\delta_{k_0,n}^2\), this is \(\delta_{k_0,n}^{2\bar\beta/(1+\bar\beta)}\), with the \(\beta>1\) saturation of Tan--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.13.
statements.justification: The calibration imports standard causal identification and records the observable holdout cost.
statements.gap: It is an equivalence calibration, not a claimed improvement over Tan and Syrgkanis.
statements.consumer: It checks that exact-closure NPIV applications recover the known saturated benchmark.

statements.statement: In \(\texttt{def:two-coordinate-diagonal}\), \(T\) is the identity on \(\mathcal H^\circ\), \(h^\dagger=h_0=a_0U+b_0V\), and target approximation is zero. For \(\mathcal F_1^\circ\), witness deficiency is zero; for \(\mathcal F_2^\circ\), \(\varepsilon_{F,2}^2\ge b_0^2>0\), while no learned-operator error is present. This bounded nondegenerate law violates exact witness closeness while satisfying target realizability and is in the positive-witness-deficiency domain of \(\texttt{conj:validated-misspecified-trae}\).
statements.justification: The construction isolates a residual coordinate omitted by a critic.
statements.gap: Li et al. (2024, Theorem 12) separate target and learned-operator errors; neither represents critic blindness when the operator is exact.
statements.consumer: It provides a diagnostic for witness enrichment in minimax inverse estimation.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{ass:diagonal-dimension}\), for the diagonal ellipsoid, the alternatives \(\theta^\omega\), full target class \(\mathcal H_{m_n,m_n}\), restricted witness class \(\mathcal F_{m_n,m_n}\), Gaussian training and validation scores, and Borel split selectors in \(\texttt{def:witness-floor-handle}\), can Assouad's method establish a constant \(c>0\) such that every \(\widehat\theta\in\mathscr S_n\) has \[\sup_{\omega\in\{-1,1\}^{|B_n|}}\mathcal R_n(\widehat\theta,\theta^\omega)\ge c|B_n|\gamma_n^2,\] and can a companion cutoff family determine whether the displayed \(\varepsilon_{F,m_n}^2/m_n^{-2a}\) and \(\varepsilon_{H,k}^2\) coordinates are jointly unavoidable for this selector class?
statements.justification: The question tests whether critic-blindness amplification is information-theoretic rather than an upper-bound artifact.
statements.gap: Neither adaptive TRAE nor misspecified RDIV gives a lower bound for a residual block annihilated by an adversarial witness class.
statements.consumer: Its resolution determines whether selectors must explicitly trade target approximation against witness deficiency.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from \(P\), followed by a deterministic balanced training--validation split.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X_i\) is endogenous and \(Z_i\) defines the NPIV conditional moment.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is used; inverse regularity is expressed through the source condition and the derived conditional-expectation contraction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The operator is not explicitly estimated. A countable, measurable adversarial TRAE path is trained on one split and scored by an independent holdout adversarial Tikhonov loss.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.13 gives discrepancy-selected TRAE adaptive rates under target realizability and exact witness closeness, with saturation for \(\beta>1\).
Theorem 12 and Section 8 give misspecified RDIV bounds and validation model selection with target-class and learned-operator approximation terms.
The paper analyzes fixed-tuning adversarial Tikhonov estimators under exact inverse equations for source-condition double-robust inference.
Localized-Rademacher minimax analysis controls conditional-moment estimation with sufficiently rich witnesses.
A constrained minimax IV estimator gives strong convergence with general function approximation under realizability.

tldr: Adaptive TRAE has exact-target and exact-witness theory but no established misspecified validation result. The central conjecture targets a wholly observable split-sample adversarial Tikhonov selector whose countable least-index training path is measurable and whose simultaneous oracle comparison separately charges target approximation and witness blindness. Under a valid and complete NPIV calibration, its pseudo-true target equals the causal structural response; under moment failure, it is only a sensitivity projection. A bounded two-coordinate theorem separates critic blindness from learned-operator error, and a specified Gaussian diagonal question asks whether inverse amplification is unavoidable.

project_justification.gap: Tan and Syrgkanis, Remark 3.8, leave approximation error outside discrepancy calibration, and Theorem 3.13 assumes target realizability and exact witness closeness. Li et al. validate misspecified explicit-operator RDIV, but not a TRAE critic blind to residual directions.
project_justification.niche: The misspecified adversarial inverse problem has an attained pseudo-true projection, target-class approximation, and witness deficiency. The last is an implicit-critic defect, and an observable selector must avoid tuning with its unknown population radius while still being measurable.
project_justification.fill: The proposal fixes a countable least-index training algorithm, a holdout adversarial validation statistic, and a simultaneous \(\eta/(2K|\Lambda_n|)\) training allocation. The headline conjecture targets their oracle comparison, the domain-separation theorem exhibits a nonzero-defect law outside exact-witness TRAE, and the diagonal question supplies explicit Gaussian scores and an Assouad handle.

related_work: Tan and Syrgkanis (2026, Theorem 3.13 and Remark 3.8) are the exact-specification benchmark; Proposition \(\texttt{prop:zero-defect-calibration}\) conditionally recovers its saturated rate with an observable holdout cost and makes no tightening claim. Li, Lan, Syrgkanis, Wang, and Uehara (2024, Theorem 12 and Section 8) provide the misspecified validation architecture for explicit-operator RDIV. The bounded domain-separation theorem shows why their learned-operator term cannot represent a missing adversarial witness coordinate. Bennett, Kallus, Mao, Newey, Syrgkanis, and Uehara (2023, Source Condition DR) are the closest fixed-tuning exact-witness TRAE ancestor and inform the adversarial Tikhonov geometry. Dikkala, Lewis, Mackey, and Syrgkanis (2020) supply localized-Rademacher tools for the implicit witness loss. Bennett et al. (2023, Minimax IV) supply the standard NPIV identification calibration. Ai and Chen (2007) motivate pseudo-true centering under conditional-moment misspecification.
honest_scope: The validated misspecified TRAE oracle inequality is a conjecture. The exact branch is a conditional calibration of that conjecture, not an established new adaptive rate; it matches the Tan--Syrgkanis saturated benchmark only if the displayed finite grid reaches the oracle scale and the holdout scale is dominated by the training scale. Under valid IV and completeness, \(h^\dagger=h_0\) is causal without a separate pseudo-true-attainment premise; under moment failure, the attained projection is only a sensitivity target. The diagonal Assouad question remains open, and no minimax-sharpness claim is made for the defect terms.
